pr.title: Plan expanding the hidden lines around a summary's diff hunks
pr.head: 4dc37bb8ddbd7ea1fbbf6a95930413997aa7d7a7

summary: A summary page is the guided review page that Projector's site serves for a pull request: the diff split into groups, with notes. Today it shows each changed file only as its diff hunks, the changed lines plus three unchanged lines around them. A reader who needs the rest of a function, or the lines between two nearby hunks, has to leave the page for GitHub.

This pull request adds one file, a plan at status: ready and priority: next. It proposes that a reader can reveal the hidden unchanged lines above, between, and below each hunk, twenty lines a click, as GitHub's diff view does. No code changes yet.

1. Publish stores the head's files. project summary publish writes, beside each summary on the hidden refs/projector/summaries ref, a tree entry for each eligible changed file that points at the head commit's existing blob. The ref gains entries but no new file content.
  2. The site build checks and serves them. The build compares each stored file with the diff's lines, writes each distinct file once under reviews/blobs/ by its Git blob id, and records the hidden gaps in the page data.
  3. The page fetches on demand. The first expand of a file fetches it, highlights it, and inserts the revealed lines as context rows.

cards.title: Review status at this head
cards.html:
The Projector review of 4dc37bb8d requested changes with two findings, shown as flags under the lines they concern:

  • The line check in § 2.2 rejects every CRLF file, because the diff text has its \r removed and the stored file keeps it.
  • The blob URL format omits the site's base path, so it 404s on a project Pages site such as this repository's.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Gap: a run of unchanged head lines the diff does not show, above the first hunk, between two hunks, or below the last.
  • Summaries ref: refs/projector/summaries, a hidden ref that holds each summary, its diff, and its attributes under summaries/<number>/<head>/.
  • Base path: the path GitHub Pages serves a site under, /projector/ for this repository.

groups.title: The plan
groups.kicker: One new project plan under docs/projects, ready to implement in two pull requests
intro: The plan follows the repository's project model: numbered sections, problem before solution, and a ready status that claims every blocking question is answered or deferred. Section 7 defers the standalone project site page, whole-file highlighting of hunks, and pruning of the summaries ref.

Read § 2 against the code it names. Publish already fetches a missing head for its attributes, the build already prefixes its URLs with the site's base path, and the page already has the highlighting helpers the plan reuses.

files.note: The whole change: the problem, the publish, build, and page design, the acceptance criteria, cost, rollout, and what is deferred.

checks.text: project check prints Project plans are valid. at this head, and project show summary-diff-context reports status: ready and priority: next.

publish_attributes in src/projector/summary.py fetches the head into the checkout when it is missing, and summary_tree keeps entries from the parent tree that it does not overwrite. Read at this head. So a republish with an unreadable head keeps earlier head/ entries, as this paragraph says.

Every CRLF file fails this check and loses its context. gh reads the compare diff with text=True, and build_summaries reads diff.patch with read_text, and both turn into . The stored file split on keeps the . A reproduction against parse_diff at this head mismatched every compared line of a CRLF file. Fix: translate to before the split, and test a CRLF file in criterion 3.

This URL has no base path. GitHub Pages serves this repository's site under /projector/, and build_summaries prefixes every other URL with base. A fetch of /reviews/blobs/… there returns 404. Tests at the default base / and project site serve would not catch it. Fix: use <base>reviews/blobs/<id>.txt, and build criterion 3's test with a non-root base.
parse_diff today keeps each hunk's header text and its lines, and reads the start numbers only to number lines. This paragraph adds the four header numbers to each hunk so the build can compute gaps.
hl, splitLines, and markTokens live in the page's wiring code, while numbers and esc are local to rendering. The expander needs both, so expect the page pull request to move some of them.
